title: The Large Plane Trees (Road Menders at Saint-Rémy)

image.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the Hanna Fund

work.text: The last study I did is a view of the village, where they were at work - under some enormous plane trees - repairing the pavements. So there are heaps of sand, stones and gigantic trunks - the leaves yellowing and here and there you get a glimpse of a house front and small figures.

source.author: Vincent van Gogh
source.title: Letter 618 to Theo van Gogh, Saint-Rémy, 7 December 1889
source.publisher: The Complete Letters of Vincent van Gogh, via WebExhibits

moment.text: Limited access to life outside the clinic resulted in a shortage of subject matter. Van Gogh instead worked on interpretations of other artist's paintings, such as Millet's The Sower and Noonday Rest, and variations on his own earlier work.

matters.text: Vincent van Gogh painted this autumnal landscape while living in a psychiatric hospital near Saint-Rémy in southern France where he was treated for severe depression. Understanding that painting from nature eased his symptoms, Van Gogh’s physician permitted the artist to paint landscapes outside.
